title: Kielbasa

items.raw: 2 pounds smoked kielbasa, cut into 3-inch lengths
1½ pounds small Yukon Gold potatoes, halved
1 pound sauerkraut, drained (rinsed if you want it milder)
1 tablespoon whole-grain mustard, plus more to serve
Freshly ground black pepper and chopped parsley

steps.text: Score the pieces lightly. Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the kielbasa on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes. Set aside.
Add the butter and onions to the pan and cook over medium heat 10 to 12 minutes, until soft and golden.
Stir in the potatoes, sauerkraut, caraway, brown sugar, beer or stock, and mustard. Nestle the kielbasa on top.
Cover and simmer on low 25 to 30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced.
Uncover and cook 5 minutes more to cook off most of the liquid. Season with pepper — the sausage and sauerkraut bring plenty of salt.
Scatter with parsley and pass more mustard at the table.

notes.label: Grilled version
notes.text: grill whole links over medium heat 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until hot through and charred, and serve on rolls with mustard and sauerkraut.

notes.label: Sauerkraut
notes.text: the refrigerated kind in bags tastes fresher than canned. Rinse it only if you want it milder.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: it reheats well and tastes even better the next day.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — kielbasa browned and braised in one pan with onions, sauerkraut, and potatoes. How is your family’s kielbasa cooked (grilled, simmered in beer, with pierogi)? Is it homemade or a particular brand or butcher? Who makes it, and for what occasion?
